function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted).
• “No Speed Limit” zones: 70 mph on some rural roads. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “no‑seat‑belt” laws for drivers. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % for drivers 21+.
• Lower limits for commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield” signs: give way to traffic in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.003 | | **School Bus** | • Stop for all vehicles when a school bus stops with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• No passing on either side. | Texas Transportation Code §545.004 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other drivers.
• “Lane‑Change” signs: use caution. | Texas Transportation Code §545.005 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a “no parking” zone is a ticket. | Texas Transportation Code §545.006 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only for vehicles that are unsafe or obstructing traffic.
• Towing a vehicle without a permit is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.007 | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens.
• Do not block intersections. | Texas Transportation Code §545.008 | | **Roadside Assistance & Hazards** | • Pull over to a safe spot if you have a breakdown.
• Use hazard lights if you cannot move. | Texas Transportation Code §545.009 | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles: must wear helmets (unless under 18).
• Commercial trucks: must follow specific lane and speed regulations. | Texas Transportation Code §545.010 | | **Penalties & Enforcement** | • Fines vary by offense.
• Points added to driver’s record can lead to license suspension.
• Repeat offenders face harsher penalties. | Texas Transportation Code §545.011 | ### How to Stay Updated - **TxDOT Website** – for changes in speed limits, construction updates, and road conditions. - **Texas DMV** – for registration, inspection, and licensing updates. - **Texas Transportation Code** – the official legal text; available online through the Texas Legislature’s website. ### Quick Tips 1. **Always obey posted signs** – they’re the law. 2. **Use hands‑free** – keep your phone out of reach while driving. 3. **Check your vehicle’s inspection status** – a failed inspection can lead to a ticket. 4. **Know the school bus rules** – stopping for a school bus is mandatory. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
